heard: A classified military mirror is about to outscan the Hubble telescope. In 2012, the National Reconnaissance Office surprised NASA by donating two 2.4-meter surveillance mirrors. NASA's first chief of astronomy, Nancy Grace Roman, inspired the team to use this hardware. Engineers adapted the reconnaissance optics into a massive flagship observatory for the 2020s. On August 30, 2026, a SpaceX Falcon Heavy carried this former spy tool to a point 1.5 million kilometers from Earth. The Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope matches Hubble's resolution, but captures an area 100 times larger. It will scan more of the sky in five years than Hubble did in over 30. This allows the observatory to hunt for thousands of exoplanets using a classified military mirror.
